gaps.sentence: Come ___ it may, the trial must proceed.
gaps.explanation: 'Come what may' — fixed inverted idiom = whatever happens.

gaps.sentence: Rarely ___ a debut film attracted such wide attention.
gaps.explanation: 'Rarely has a debut film attracted …' — perfect inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not once ___ she mentioned the incident to anyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Not once has she mentioned' — inversion with the perfect.

gaps.sentence: Also worth ___ is the museum's medieval wing.
gaps.explanation: Also worth noting is… — fronted comment structure.

gaps.sentence: Not until the second edition ___ the book become a bestseller.
gaps.explanation: 'Not until the second edition did the book become …'.

gaps.sentence: Only by practising daily ___ you improve your fluency.
gaps.explanation: Only by doing X will you… — future inversion after only by.

gaps.sentence: Not until the film ended ___ anybody speak.
gaps.explanation: Not until + time clause at the front: did anybody speak.

gaps.sentence: ___ the storm passed did the ferries resume service.
gaps.explanation: Only after/once the storm passed did… — fronted 'only' phrase.
